before.title: Spectral completeness of the curl operator in a smooth PEC cavity
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the complete variational, Sobolev-extension and compact-spectral suppliers. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\}$ and $H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$ with their graph norms, and let $X$ be the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$; this is an explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor boundary class. Put $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline{V}^{\,L^2}$. Then the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and must be retained when the topology allows it. The eigen equation is $$\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$$ distributionally with the PEC trace, and for the associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ the coefficients solve $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, with convergence in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data and the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes linear in time. No identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no lossy, open or non-smooth-domain spectral claim, is made.
before.strategy:
Compactness and $H^1$ equivalence. For smooth $u$ with $n	imes u=0$, expanding $|\operatorname{curl}u|^2$ and integrating once gives $\int_\Omega(|\operatorname{curl}u|^2+|\operatorname{div}u|^2-|
abla u|^2)=\int_{\partial\Omega}(\operatorname{div}n)|u\cdot n|^2dS$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] and the divergence theorem on the collar). The curvature is bounded on the compact smooth boundary, and the collar normal-line identity $|u(y,0)|^2=|u(y,t)|^2-\int_0^t\partial_s|u|^2ds$ with $2ab\le\delta a^2+\delta^{-1}b^2$ gives $\|u\|_{L^2(\partial\Omega)}^2\le\delta\|
abla u\|_2^2+C_\delta\|u\|_2^2$; absorbing the curvature term yields $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|u\|_2+\|\operatorname{curl}u\|_2+\|\operatorname{div}u\|_2)$, so the completion $X$ is a closed $H^1$ subspace with zero tangential trace by trace continuity. The $H^1$ inclusion in $L^2$ is compact by the elementary cube-averaging proof using the bounded smooth-domain extension ([[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]]): for a bounded family of extensions the rectangular mean estimate gives uniform $\|u-P_hu\|_2\le Ch\|
abla u\|_2$ with $P_h$ of finite-dimensional range, so a finite $\varepsilon$-net exists in total bounded and complete $L^2$. The shifted form $a(u,v)=\int[\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v+u\cdot v]$ is coercive and complete, so the symmetric solver ([[lem-em-symmetric-coercive-variational-solver]]) defines $K_0$; if $f$ is distributionally divergence-free and $q=\operatorname{div}K_0f$, testing with $v=
abla\varphi$ gives $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=0$ for all smooth zero-trace $\varphi$, and the local Dirichlet resolvent and smooth-zero-boundary test-density lemma ([[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]]) gives the unique $\varphi\in H^2\cap H_0^1$ solving $(1-\Delta)\varphi=q$. Its smooth zero-boundary approximants $\varphi_j$ converge in $H^2$, so $
abla\varphi_j$ are smooth PEC fields converging to $
abla\varphi$ in the curl/div graph norm, proving this gradient belongs to the chosen completion $X$. The identity for smooth $\varphi_j$ passes by $L^2$ continuity to $\int q(\Delta\varphi-\varphi)=-\|q\|_2^2=0$; hence $K=K_0|_H$ maps $H$ into $V$ and is bounded $H	o V$ and compact $H	o H$ ([[def-compact-linear-operator]]). Testing its defining equations with $Kg,Kf$ proves self-adjointness, and $(f,Kf)=\|\operatorname{curl}Kf\|^2+\|Kf\|^2>0$ for $f
e0$ proves trivial kernel. The compact self-adjoint spectral theorem ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators]]) now gives an orthonormal eigenbasis of $H$ with positive eigenvalues $\kappa_j	o0$ of finite multiplicity; substituting $Ku_j=\kappa_ju_j$ into the full $X$ identity gives $\int\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=(\kappa_j^{-1}-1)\int u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, and testing with compactly supported $v$ gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with $\lambda_j=\kappa_j^{-1}-1\ge0$, the zero eigenspace being finite dimensional by the spectral theorem. The wave statement is the standard coefficient decomposition $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with finite-sum energy convergence, exactly as in the rectangular case, retaining the finitely many $\lambda=0$ linear modes.

after.title: Smooth boundary regularity of PEC cavity eigenfields in the declared graph completion
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, and let $X$ be exactly the curl/div graph-norm completion of smooth-on-the-closure fields with $
u	imes u=0$ defined in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]. If $u\in X$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ weakly, and $\lambda\ge0$ satisfies $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$, then $u\in H^m(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ for every integer $m\ge1$ and has a $C^\infty$ representative on the closure (indeed a smooth ambient extension to a neighbourhood of the closure). For each $m$, $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$. The equations $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $
u	imes u=0$ and $\partial_
u u_n+(\operatorname{div}
u)u_n=0$ hold classically, where $u_n=u\cdot
u$ and the normal is extended constant along collar normal lines. This includes zero eigenvalues and disconnected domains; it asserts neither equality with every maximal tangential-trace realization nor smoothness of arbitrary finite-energy modal sums.
after.strategy:
1. Bilinear boundary identity in the chosen completion. Write $
u$ for the outward unit normal, extend it smoothly as a unit field in a collar, put $\kappa=\operatorname{div}
u$ on the boundary, and write $u_n=u\cdot
u$. Polarizing the identity proved in [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]] gives, for smooth PEC $u,v$,
$$\int_\Omega(\operatorname{curl}u\cdot\operatorname{curl}v+\operatorname{div}u\operatorname{div}v)=\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v+\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa u_n v_n.$$
For clarity the integration-by-parts boundary term before imposing the traces is $\sum_{i,j}\int_{\partial\Omega}(
u_j u_j\partial_i v_i-
u_j u_i\partial_i v_j)$; at the boundary $u=u_n
u$, $v=v_n
u$, the tangential derivatives of $v$ and $
u\cdot\partial_i
u=0$ reduce it to $\kappa u_n v_n$. Thus the sign is positive for an outward convex sphere ($\kappa=2/R$); no convexity is assumed. The $H^1$ norm equivalence of that supplier and the bounded trace [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] extend this identity from smooth PEC approximants to every pair in the actual graph completion $X$. Since $\operatorname{div}u=0$, the assumed full-$X$ eigenidentity therefore gives
$$\int_\Omega
abla u:
abla v+\int_{\partial\Omega}\kappa u_n v_n=\lambda\int_\Omega u\cdot v\qquad(v\in X).$$
This is the weak mixed boundary identity; no classical normal derivative has yet been assumed.

2. Flattening and actual admissibility. Shrink smooth boundary charts before taking a finite cover of the compact boundary, with nested half-boxes and cutoffs away from artificial sides. In each chart choose a smooth orthonormal frame $Q=(	au_1,	au_2,
u)$ on the boundary, by normalizing a graph tangent and putting $	au_2=
u	imes	au_1$, and extend it smoothly into the collar. In flattened coordinates $(y_1,y_2,s)$ with $s>0$ inside, write $u=QU$. The $H^1$ trace has $TU_1=TU_2=0$; $TU_3$ is free. Every localized $H^1$ triple $V$ with these two zero traces and compact support away from the artificial sides pulls back to an element of the original $X$: extend $V_1,V_2$ oddly and $V_3$ evenly across $s=0$. These are $H^1$ extensions. Indeed integrating against a smooth test on both half-spaces cancels the interface term for equal one-sided traces; the odd extensions have matching traces because their traces are zero, and the even extension has matching traces automatically. This is the first-order gluing calculation in [[lem-em-dirichlet-resolvent-h-two-and-smooth-test-density]] and the half-space trace integration argument of [[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]]. Mollify with a compact kernel even in $s$; convolution preserves these parities, converges in $H^1$, and makes the first two traces exactly zero. Multiply by an even smooth cutoff equal to one on the localized support and pull back through the smooth frame and chart. Extend by zero outside the chart. The resulting fields are smooth on the closure, have $
u	imes v_j=0$ exactly, and converge to the localized field in $H^1$, hence in the curl/div graph norm. This explicitly supplies the smooth PEC approximants required by the definition of $X$. Interior compactly supported tests are obtained by ordinary mollification. This local construction is used below; no equality with an unspecified maximal tangential-trace realization is asserted.

3. The local coupled weak system. Expanding $
abla(QU)$ in the identity of step 1 and transporting the volume measure gives a real symmetric smooth principal matrix $a^{ij}$, uniformly positive on the smaller half-box, that is scalar in the three component indices. The frame derivative terms have smooth matrix coefficients and at most one derivative of $U$. Thus the local equation for all admissible triples $V$ is
$$\sum_m\int a^{ij}\partial_jU_m\partial_iV_m+\int_B eta U_3V_3=\int f\cdot V+\sum_i\int G_i\cdot\partial_iV,$$
where $B=\{s=0\}$, $ eta=\kappa J_B$ is smooth (possibly signed), $f=\lambda JU+\sum_i C_i\partial_iU+C_0U\in L^2$, and $G_i=B_iU\in H^1$ for smooth matrix coefficients $C_i,C_0,B_i$; $J$ and $J_B$ are the positive volume and surface densities. This follows directly by expanding the finite products: the only two differentiated factors produce the scalar $a^{ij}$ because $Q^TQ=I$; terms with a derivative of $Q$ on the test factor enter $G$, and those with a derivative of $Q$ on the solution factor enter $f$. Multipliers obey [[lem-cutoff-difference-quotient-commutator-estimate]]. More generally allow a boundary datum $\int_B hV_3$ with $h\in H^1(B)$ for the induction below. Localization $Z=\eta U$ has the same principal and Robin terms and exactly $f_Z=\eta f+\sum_i G_i\partial_i\eta-\sum_{i,j}a^{ij}\partial_jU\partial_i\eta$, $G_{Z,i}=\eta G_i+\sum_j a^{ij}U\partial_j\eta$, and $h_Z=\eta h$. In particular the divergence-type cutoff/frame terms are retained rather than silently assigning zero conormal data.

4. Tangential mixed $H^2$ estimate. Let $k=1,2$, set $W=\delta_h^k U=(U(y+he_k,s)-U(y,s))/h$, and test with $V=-\delta_{-h}^k(\eta^2W)$ on a nested patch. For each fixed small $h$, its first two traces vanish; step 2 makes its pullback an admissible element of $X$ by actual smooth PEC approximation. Discrete integration by parts and the shifted product rule give the principal term $\sum_m\int\eta^2 a^{ij}(x+he_k)\partial_jW_m\partial_iW_m\ge\alpha\|\eta
abla W\|_2^2$. The other principal terms involve $\delta_h a$, $
abla\eta$, $
abla U$ and $W$ and are bounded by $\epsilon\|\eta
abla W\|_2^2+C_\epsilon\|U\|_{H^1}^2$ on the larger patch. The elementary line formula $\delta_h U=\int_0^1\partial_kU(x+the_k)dt$, valid on a.e. ACL line, and Cauchy--Schwarz in $t$ followed by Fubini give $\|W\|_2\le C\|\partial_kU\|_2$ on the enlarged patch; it also bounds $\|\delta_{-h}(\eta^2W)\|_2$ by $C(\|\eta
abla W\|_2+\|W\|_2)$. Hence the $f$ term is bounded without differentiating $f$. Transfer the quotient in the $G$ pairing to $G$; $\|\delta_hG\|_2\le C\|G\|_{H^1}$ gives the same bound. On $B$ the exact quotient of the Robin product gives $\int_B eta(y+h)\eta^2|W_3|^2+\int_B(\delta_h eta)U_3\eta^2W_3$. The normal-line proof in G3 gives the localized trace estimate $\|Tz\|_2^2\le\epsilon\|
abla z\|_2^2+C_\epsilon\|z\|_2^2$. It absorbs the first term even when $ eta$ has either sign; bounded $\delta_h eta$, $\|TU_3\|_2\le C\|U\|_{H^1}$ and Young bound the second in the same way. The extra $h$ pairing transfers to $\delta_h h$ and is bounded by $\|h\|_{H^1(B)}\|T(\eta^2W_3)\|_2$, again absorbed by the trace estimate and Young. Choosing the finitely many epsilons small relative to $\alpha$ yields
$$\|\eta
abla\delta_h^kU\|_2\le C(\|U\|_{H^1}+\|f\|_2+\|G\|_{H^1}+\|h\|_{H^1(B)}),$$
uniformly for small $h$. These estimates apply to all three components and explicitly bound the coupled lower-order and Robin terms; a scalar Dirichlet theorem has not been substituted for this system.

5. Recover normal derivatives. From the last bound each distributional tangential derivative of $\partial_iU_m$ is $L^2$: for a smooth test $\psi$ its pairing is the limit of $\int\delta_h^k(\partial_iU_m)\psi$, a bounded $L^2$ functional, represented by an $L^2$ class (Hilbert Riesz, available through the variational supplier in G3). Interior quotient tests give the same conclusion away from the boundary. The interior equation is $-\partial_i(a^{ij}\partial_jU_m)=f_m-\partial_iG_{i,m}$. Therefore
$$a^{33}\partial_{33}U_m=\partial_iG_{i,m}-f_m-\sum_{(i,j)
e(3,3)}a^{ij}\partial_{ij}U_m-\sum_{i,j}(\partial_i a^{ij})\partial_jU_m.$$
Every term on the right is $L^2$, and $a^{33}\ge\alpha>0$, so all three normal second derivatives are $L^2$. This proves local $H^2$ with a bound on a smaller patch. It does not require a pre-existing classical Robin derivative.

6. Full bootstrap with boundary commutators. Suppose $U\in H^{r+1}$ on the larger patch, $r\ge1$. Its actual lower-order data satisfy $f\in H^r$ and $G\in H^{r+1}$, since the equation's eigenvalue term is $\lambda JU$ and all coefficients are smooth; no initially smooth right-hand side is presumed. For a tangential multi-index $\alpha$ of order $r$, put $Z=D_y^\alpha U\in H^1$. Its first two traces are still zero. To justify trace commutation, extend any localized $H^{r+1}$ class by the integer-order half-space extension [[thm-wkp-extension-from-a-half-space]], mollify in that norm, and use the continuous $H^1$ trace for every derivative of order at most $r$; the smooth tangential trace identity passes to the limit. Apply tangential integration by parts to the weak system of step 3. Its principal term remains $a^{ij}\partial_j Z_m\partial_iV_m$, its boundary principal term remains $ eta Z_3V_3$, its bulk datum is $D_y^\alpha f\in L^2$, and its divergence-type datum is
$$\widetilde G_i=D_y^\alpha G_i-\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\gamma}(D_y^\gamma a^{ij})\partial_jD_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U\in H^1.$$
The boundary commutator is $\widetilde h=-\sum_{0<\gamma\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\gamma}(D_y^\gamma eta)T D_y^{\alpha-\gamma}U_3\in H^1(B)$. Indeed $|\alpha-\gamma|\le r-1$, so the indicated derivative of $U$ is $H^2$; its trace and each tangential derivative trace are $L^2$ by the $H^1$ trace and its just-proved commutation. This proves the claimed $H^1(B)$ bound without assuming a stronger trace theorem. Step 2 again makes localized tests for $Z$ admissible by smooth PEC approximation; differentiation of the weak identity is justified first by difference quotients and then distributional limits. Steps 4--5 give $Z\in H^2$, controlling derivatives of total order $r+2$ with at most two normal derivatives. For the remaining derivatives, differentiate the normal-recovery equation of step 5 and induct on the number of normal derivatives at this fixed total order. The non-$(3,3)$ principal terms have strictly fewer normal derivatives; all differentiated coefficient terms use derivatives of $U$ of order at most $r+1$, and differentiated $f$ and $\operatorname{div}G$ have that same available order. Dividing by positive $a^{33}$ recovers the next normal derivative. Thus $U\in H^{r+2}$. Use nested patches for each finite order and the finite boundary/interior cover to obtain $u\in H^m(\Omega)$ for every integer $m$, with $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$; no estimate uniform in $\lambda$ is asserted.

7. Classical conclusion. For each $j$ choose $m>j+3/2$ and apply [[thm-extension-theorem-for-bounded-smooth-domains]] and [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]] componentwise. They yield continuous derivatives through order $j$ on the closure, compatible for different $j$ by weak derivative uniqueness and continuity on the interior. All jets therefore have continuous one-sided boundary limits. The fixed smooth extension [[lem-em-parameter-preserving-smooth-extension-on-a-smooth-domain]] applied to the constant-in-time field gives one actual smooth ambient representative near the entire closure, rather than unrelated finite-order extensions. The interior variational equation gives $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$ pointwise, and the tangential trace is classically zero. Now integration by parts in step 1 with arbitrary smooth compactly supported normal boundary traces, admissible by step 2, gives $\partial_
u u_n+\kappa u_n=0$ pointwise. The unit-normal collar extension ensures $\partial_
u u_n=(\partial_
u u)\cdot
u$ when the normal is extended constant along its normal lines. This agrees with the classical identity $\operatorname{div}u=\partial_
u u_n+\kappa u_n$ for zero tangential trace. The argument covers $\lambda=0$, disconnected smooth domains, and every topology allowed by G3; it makes no smoothness assertion for arbitrary finite-energy modal sums. Full AC is carried from G3, the trace, extension, Hilbert and Sobolev suppliers. Hunter's bounded scalar Dirichlet excerpt supports the difference-quotient method only; the vector coupling, actual graph-class tests and Robin bootstrap above are proved locally here.

references.title: J. K. Hunter, Notes on Partial Differential Equations (UC Davis): scalar boundary difference-quotient method; the vector Robin extension is proved inline here

before.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. The associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ has coefficients $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, converges in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data, and retains the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The classical smoothness of the eigenfields on the declared smooth domain, and the solvability of the shifted auxiliary boundary problems used in the construction, are those supplied by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] on $\Omega$.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For a rectangular box the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
before.strategy: The smooth-cavity assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]], whose proof constructs the compact self-adjoint solution operator of the shifted problem with the coercive solver and the smooth-domain interior estimate, applies the compact self-adjoint spectral theorem to obtain the eigenbasis and the multiplicities, and derives the distributional eigen-equation and the modal wave expansion with zero modes retained. This item records the composition with the elliptic existence theorem of this page: [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] supplies the weak solvability and the classical ($C^\infty$-on-the-closure) upgrade on the bounded smooth domain for the elliptic boundary problems used in the closure argument, so the eigenfields and the auxiliary problems live on the declared smooth class; the quadratic graph forms and the curl/div expressions are computed with the calculus conventions of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and the Euclidean inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. The rectangular assertions are the recorded $G2$ content of [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]]: the reflection parities convert the boundary class into a rectangular torus class, the imported one-dimensional complete trigonometric system and Hilbert Fourier expansion give product completeness, and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE with conservation of $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$ gives the unique weak solution and energy conservation; the direct TE/TM mode verification is the recorded physics branch G1 on the guide page and is not a mathematical dependency here. The recorded K10 branch (uniform Ohmic loss) is a physical-model branch of the same modal argument and is homed on the physical page, not here.

after.title: Spectral completeness of the declared PEC waveguide and cavity classes
after.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the explicitly used variational, Sobolev and compact-spectral suppliers. Let the PEC classes be those of [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: for a bounded $C^\infty$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$, $X$ is the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$, $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline V^{\,L^2}$. Then:
(a) **Smooth cavity.** The curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis $\{u_j\}$ with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity, $\lambda_j\to\infty$ whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and a finite-dimensional zero eigenspace that is retained; the eigen-equation $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ holds distributionally with the PEC trace. The associated second-order wave with initial displacement in $V$ and velocity in $H$ has coefficients $a_j''+c^2\lambda_ja_j=0$, converges in $C_tV\cap C_tH$ for finite-energy data, and retains the finitely many $\lambda=0$ modes $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. The eigenfields are $C^\infty$ on the closure by [[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]], applied to the full-$X$ eigenvariational identity of the cavity supplier. The shifted scalar auxiliary boundary problems are solvable on the declared bounded smooth domain by [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]]; the specific scalar Dirichlet resolvent and its smooth-zero-boundary test density used in G3 are supplied by its recorded local resolvent lemma.
(b) **Rectangular class.** For a rectangular box the separable products described in the mode verification are dense in the reflection-parity energy class, and every initial datum of that class has a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the class with constant energy, with finite separated modes dense at every time. The rectangular statements are the recorded rectangular reflection-class completeness lemma [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (the $G2$ branch); the individual TE/TM mode verification against the Maxwell equations and the PEC conditions is the recorded $G1$ physics branch, homed on the physical guide page and not consumed here as a mathematical premise. No completeness in lossy, open-ended or non-smooth classes is asserted.
after.strategy: The smooth-cavity spectral and finite-energy assertions are exactly [[lem-em-smooth-pec-cavity-spectral-closure]]: its shifted coercive full-$X$ solution operator, divergence projection using the proved scalar Dirichlet resolvent and smooth-zero-boundary density, and compact self-adjoint spectral theorem give the complete $H^1$ graph-class eigenbasis, multiplicities, distributional equations and modal wave expansion with topology zero modes retained. Each eigenfield satisfies its full-$X$ variational identity, so [[lem-em-pec-cavity-eigenfield-boundary-regularity]] gives the promised $C^\infty$ eigenfields on the closure, including $\lambda=0$. That supplier proves the coupled vector mixed boundary estimate and admissible tests in the chosen completion; the scalar [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]] is used only for its actual scalar auxiliary boundary solvability and is not treated as a vector PEC regularity theorem. The quadratic graph forms and curl/div expressions use [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. No classical smoothness of general finite-energy sums follows or is asserted. The rectangular assertions are unchanged [[lem-em-rectangular-pec-energy-completeness]] (G2): reflection parities give the rectangular torus class; trigonometric product completeness and the finite-dimensional Fourier ODE conserve $\varepsilon|\hat E|^2+|\hat B|^2/\mu$, yielding the unique weak energy solution. The direct TE/TM verification G1 and uniform Ohmic-loss branch K10 remain physical branches on their own page, not mathematical premises here.
